name: Núi Bà Đen (Black Virgin Mountain)
alternateNames: The Mountain (what Larry and his unit called it)
"Sun Mountain" (as first written down in the family brief)
summary: An isolated mountain rising from the plain near Tây Ninh. "They called the camp The Mountain. The guys in my Unit in Saigon called it the mountain." Larry went up by helicopter for stints of a week or ten days, sometimes two back to back: "I liked it there. It was safer there." Asked what the camp was for, he said: "The best place to have readios because it was high." He ran the radio there, stood by for search and rescue at the Special Forces camp, call sign Body Jab 42, near the old French fort, and photographed a rocket launcher being set up on the summit (VN-0006). He ran sick call for the Cambodians and their families with a New Zealand medic he called Kiwi, while "Captain Kennedy handled the political problems." He describes the residents' shelters built of scrap, "to get a stick like that you would go down into the jungle and carry it up"; the machine gun on top of the rock; the mortar pit he ran for at night when the camp was attacked; a Cambodian chief who came in wearing a necklace of thirty human ears; and the quiet: "I enjoyed being on Nui Ba Den because of it being quiet. I could read and I stayed up at night with the Special Forces guys in case we were attacked." He read James Bond, le Carré, Louis L'Amour and Zane Grey there. His last day on the mountain was the day of the "450 civilians" accusation, at the very end of his tour.
researchNotes: The mountain's location is settled geography; what remains unverified is the nature and dates of Larry's association with it. On documentary fit the association is rated plausible: the official Army history documents a small Special Forces camp at the mountain in 1964 (matching his skeleton crew), a veteran-compiled index of positions and a 1965 veteran's photograph name the camp, and the RADIX order of battle prints its mission as radio relay, which Larry gave cold on 2026-09-01. Direct confirmation of his presence awaits his NPRC records. The camp's designations, the unit sources, the French fort candidates, the summit installations and their dates are kept in research/places/nui-ba-den-locations.md, research/places/nui-ba-den-summit-installations.md and research/places/vhp-chivers-a324.md; the fuller analysis that stood in this field until 2026-09-14 is in research/places/records-cleanup-2026-09-14.md (moved after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md: unit designations stay out of records while his unit is an open cold question). "Sun Mountain" came from the founding family brief (data/recollections/2026-brief-nui-ba-den.json, paraphrase); Larry's own word is "The Mountain" (2026-09-01-phone-the-mountain-name.json). 2026-09-12, at the photographs: "The mountain is 2970 feet" (VN-0036), "It takes 27 hours to walk up the mountain" (VN-0037), a .30-calibre machine gun on top of the rock (VN-0035), and a patrol "to the left of Nui Ba Den" (VN-0023). His height is his figure; no source cited on this record gives the elevation, and the figure is not corrected. Several 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-12 paraphrases about his drawing of the mountain (VD-0002) and one 2026-09-12 comment are under hold and do not render. The rendered list of people is derived from both person and place records.
